title: Polynomial-time counted suffix
statement: Let $s$ and $u$ be polynomial-time computable functions from binary words to binary words. Then the function mapping $x$ to the suffix of $s(x)$ obtained by dropping the first $|u(x)|$ bits is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: If a word producer and a length-witness producer are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function dropping, from the produced word, a number of leading bits equal to the witness's length; each tail call is charged even after the word is exhausted.
